**Explanation:**
The writer (Franz Kafka, in this excerpt from *The Judgment*) establishes a believable world primarily through visual and tactile details. At the beginning of the passage, the narrator paints a clear picture of the setting by describing the "low, lightly built houses" that differ almost only in "height and coloring," as well as the view from the window showing the river, the bridge, and the hills on the other bank with their "faint green." There is also a sense of touch and physical grounding when Georg rests his elbow on the desk, and further visual detail when he recalls his friend's "foreign-looking full beard" and the "yellow skin color" that suggests a developing illness. While the passage does not heavily engage the senses of sound, smell, or taste—as it quickly shifts into Georg's internal thoughts—the specific visual descriptions are effective enough to make the environment and characters feel tangible and real to the reader.
